players.name: Rashid Khan
players.bio:
Afghanistan leg-spinner Rashid Khan is one of the world’s most devastating T20 bowlers.

The skilful leg-spinner has starred in short-form tournaments across the globe showcasing his unpredictable wrong’un and trademark aeroplane celebration, and has taken the BBL by storm since arriving in BBL|07.

Rashid was Adelaide’s leading wicket-taker in both BBL|07 and BBL|08 and was also voted by his teammates as the club’s Most Valuable Player in each of those seasons.

Even when not taking wickets, Rashid has proven to be one of the hardest players in the competition to get away boasting an amazing economy rate below a run a ball.

An incredible player and an extremely popular figure on and off the pitch, Rashid has signed a new deal with the Strikers for BBL|10.

players.name: Mohammad Nabi
players.didyouKnow: He is ranked in the Top 10 ODI allrounders.
players.bio:
Now captain of Afghanistan, Mohammad Nabi first picked up a cricket bat aged 10 while living in a refugee camp in Peshawar.

He honed his skills through countless hours of cricket before he began formal training at Arshad Khan’s academy in Peshawar.

An off-spinning allrounder, Nabi attracted the attention of Mike Gatting when he scored a century against a visiting MCC team and from there his career was launched.

Opportunities for MCC followed and in April 2009 Nabi played in Afghanistan’s first one-day international, scoring 58.

In his 40 ODIs since Nabi has played a major role in Afghanistan’s rise as a cricket nation and in 2010 he was appointed captain.

He has scored seven fifties including a high score of 77 against United Arab Emirates in May 2014, while Nabi’s best performance with the ball was 4-31 against Canada in 2011.

players.name: Rohit Sharma
players.didyouKnow: He scored 177 and 111 not out respectively in his first two Test matches.
players.bio:
An exciting batsman who made his international debut as a 20-year-old, Rohit Sharma has risen to captain his country in all three formats of the game.

Rohit has been a white-ball wizard for well over a decade, with three ODI double centuries to his name (including a best of 264 against Sri Lanka) and multiple IPL titles with the Mumbai Indians.

Rohit took on the Test captaincy in 2022 at the end of Virat Kohl’s reign, leading India to the World Test Championship final in 2023, which they lost to Australia.

Perhaps his legacy piece however will be his success in leading India to victory in the 2024 T20 World Cup in the Caribbean, breaking a 13-year trophy drought for the cricket-mad nation.

players.name: Shubman Gill
players.bio:
Easy on the eye and effortlessly talented, Shubman Gill was named vice-captain for India's campaign at the 2018 Under-19 World Cup.

He made his ODI debut just a year later, and a year after that was making his Test debut against Australia in the Boxing Day Test. Gill applied himself impressively in the final three Tests of that famous 2020-21 series, which saw the Indians win Down Under again against the odds.

That being said, it took time for results to come at Test level and he was given time to succeed, with his first century coming in his 23rd innings.

Once he regained his spot in the ODI in 2022, Gill's form in the 50-over format has been incredible, highlight by his 208 against New Zealand in 2023.

Gill scored the most runs in IPL 2023 (890) and had a strong ODI World Cup later that year, part of the India XI that ultimately lost to Australia in the final in Ahmedabad.

The "Prince" of Indian cricket was handed over the reins of the country's Test and ODI sides in 2025.

players.name: KL Rahul
players.didyouKnow: He enjoys rock climbing in his spare time.
players.bio:
A regular in the India top order for the best part of a decade, KL Rahul has made international centuries in all three formats.

Having made his Test debut during the 2014 Boxing Day Test, Rahul took a bit of time to find his feet at the top level. In 2016 he averaged 59.88 for the calendar year, which included his special 199 against England in Chennai.

Although an accomplished wicketkeeper, his opportunity to keep wickets for India have been rare given their strength in that field during his career.

Known for his elegant stroke play, Rahul has also proven himself to be a team man, moving up and down the batting order to accommodate his side’s needs.

He has been one of the most prolific run-scorer in the IPL. The tournament has also given him the chance to display his leadership skills, having led the Punjab Kings and the Lucknow Superchargers in the past. Rahul has also been part of the Indian leadership group and has led the team in all three formats.

players.name: Shreyas Iyer
players.bio:
A stylish middle-order batter, Shreyas Iyer has made his mark in ODI cricket for India since his debut in 2017.

The Mumbai player was part of India’s U19 World Cup side in 2014 and had impressive First-class and List A debut seasons the same year. Iyer had an equally successful debut in Indian Premier League in 2015, where he was named the Emerging Player of the Year, playing for the Delhi Daredevils.

Iyer had a dream Test debut in 2021, hitting a century in the first innings and following it with a score of 65 in the second in the match against New Zealand.

His leadership qualities were identified early in his domestic and IPL career. He led the Delhi Capitals to their first-ever IPL finals in 2020. He went one better with the Kolkata Knight Riders, winning them the title in 2024.

Iyer has devolved a successful captain- coach partnership with Ricky Ponting in the IPL. The Australian legend rates him highly and signed him up as the captain for his new team Punjab Kings ahead of the 2025 season having worked with at the Delhi Capitals previously. The duo took the Kings to the final in the very first season as Iyer became the first captain to lead three different teams to the title clash of the IPL.

Iyer was rewarded for his leadership success in domestic and IPL cricket when he was named the vice-captain of the Indian ODI side in 2025.

players.name: Washington Sundar
players.bio:
Hailing from Chennai in India’s south, Washington Sundar featured as a batting allrounder in the 2016 Under-19 World Cup as a 16-year-old.

The following year, Sundar made his IPL debut for Rising Pune Super Giants and his economical off-spin caught the eye.

By the end of 2017, his fast-tracked rise was complete, making his ODI and T20I debuts against Sri Lanka.

A really strong performance for Royal Challengers Bangalore in the 2020 IPL, where his economy rate was only 5.96 across 15 matches, helped earn him a call up to India’s Test squad that travelled to Australia at the end of the year.

Injury to fellow Tamil Nadu spinner Ravichandran Ashwin allow Sundar to make his Test debut in Brisbane in early 2021, a famous match where India chased a big fourth-innings total to secure the Border-Gavaskar Trophy.

Although he was consistently around the national T20 squad from 2019 onwards, Sundar was overlooked for the 20-over World Cups in 2021, 2022 and 2024.

The offie ended a three-and-a-half year absence from the Test team with his 7-59 against New Zealand in October 2024.

players.name: Nitish Kumar Reddy
players.bio:
Virtually unheard of before the 2024 edition of the IPL, Nitish Kumar Reddy made his name with a breakout season with the Sunrisers Hyderabad under the tutelage of Pat Cummins.

He had success as a destructive middle-order batter and his more-than-handy medium pace was used as a chop-out option.

As a 21-year-old, Reddy was named to make his Test debut in the opening Test of the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Perth.

players.name: Arshdeep Singh
players.bio:
Arshdeep Singh made his international debut in a T20I against England in 2022.

The left-arm quick has been used as a white-ball specialist by India, with his speed and ability to consistently hit the yorker length deployed to good effect in the death overs regularly.

Arshdeep made a mark on the international stage instantly, achieving the rare feat of starting with a maiden over in his first-ever match.

He has since gone on to become first and the fastest Indian bowler to take 100 wickets in Men's T20Is.

A highlight of Arshdeep's career came at the MCG in 2022. Playing his first T20 World Cup game, a high-pressure encounter against arch-rivals Pakistan, the young fast bowler removed opposition captain Babar Azam on a golden duck with his very first ball. He followed it up with the wicket of the other opener, Mohammad Rizwan, in his next over.

The Punjab player finished as the leading wicket-taker for his team in that tournament. In the next edition of the T20 World Cup in 2024, he was the overall join-highest wicket taker for the tournament, taking 17 scalps. He was also named in the ICC Team of the Tournament.

Arshdeep is currently India's highest wicket-taker in Men’s T20Is, having overtaken Yuzvendra Chahal in 2025.

players.name: Prasidh Krishna
players.bio:
Prasidh Krishna made his international debut for India in an ODI against England in 2021. Recording figures of 4 for 54, he became the first Indian bowler to claim a 4-wicket-haul on ODI debut.

His Test and T20Is debuts followed in 2023.

With his shining first-class and List A performances for Karnataka, Prasidh came to be regarded as one of the most promising young quicks in India.

He made his first-class debut for his state side against a Bangladesh A team in 2017 and took a five-for. That performance earned the then 19-year-old a call-up to MRF Pace Academy in Chennai where he was coached by Australian fast-bowling legend Glenn McGrath.

In 2019, Prasidh was invited to train under Jeff Thomson at Cricket Australia's Centre of Excellence. These experiences played a significant role in his growth as a fast bowler.

While his career has been marred by injuries that have not allowed him to establish a regular place in the Indian sides, he was been part of some significant tours for his country.

Prasidh got to play a home World Cup when he was added to India's 2023 Cricket World Cup squad as a replacement for injured allrounder Hardik Pandya.

During the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy series, he came into the Indian side in the Sydney Test in place of Jasprit Bumrah and took six Australian wickets. Later in the same year, he played three Tests on India's tour of England.
